 Follow Matthew Perry’s Sister Reveals “Friends” Cast’s Emotional Final Moments Together at His Private Funeral
 The cast “all walked in together,” Perry’s sister recalled in a new Netflix docuseries
 Julia Moore Tue, October 27, 2026 at 7:01 AM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Mia Perry Bowick in 'The One About Matthew Perry'; Matt LeBlanc, Lisa Kudrow, David Schwimmer, Matthew Perry, Courteney Cox and Jennifer Aniston in 'Friends' season 1
Credit: NETFLIX; Reisig & Taylor/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty NEED TO KNOW
 New details have been revealed about the final moments the Friends cast shared with Matthew Perry at his private funeral
 In the new Netflix docuseries The One About Matthew Perry, his sister Mia Perry Bowick speaks out for the first time and recalled seeing the cast on the emotional day in 2023
 The One About Matthew Perry is now streaming on Netflix
 New details have been revealed about the final moments the Friends cast shared with Matthew Perry .
 The actor was found dead in his Los Angeles home three years ago, in October 2023, at age 54. His cause of death was later determined to be "acute effects of ketamine ," and various people involved, including Perry's assistant Kenneth Iwamasa , have been charged and sentenced to prison for their involvement in the overdose .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In The One About Matthew Perry , a three-part docuseries that premiered on Netflix on Tuesday, Oct. 27, the actor's loved ones share insights about his inner life, his years-long battle with addiction and his death.
 Among the revelations is a never-before-shared detail about the Friends cast at Perry's funeral , which took place six days after he died.
 Jennifer Aniston , Courteney Cox , Lisa Kudrow , Matt LeBlanc and David Schwimmer were all in attendance at the service, which was held at Forest Lawn Memorial Park in Los Angeles.
 The cast of 'Friends': Courteney Cox, Matthew Perry, David Schwimmer, Jennifer Aniston, Matt LeBlanc and Lisa Kudrow 
 Credit: NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty 
 In the new docuseries, Perry's sister Mia Perry Bowick recalled seeing the cast that day. "The funeral was very small, close friends and family only. I remember sitting in the front row with our family and seeing his mom and all the other siblings," Mia shared. "And then the rest of the Friends cast all walked in together."
 Advertisement Advertisement "I hadn't seen them in easily 20 years. And Jen Aniston was the first one of them to come up to me and give me a huge hug, but they all did," Mia said. "And then all five of them walked up to the casket holding hands, and just stood around him, crying."
 In the aftermath of Perry's death, the cast shared a joint statement with PEOPLE. "We are all so utterly devastated by the loss of Matthew. We were more than just cast mates. We are a family. There is so much to say, but right now we're going to take a moment to grieve and process this unfathomable loss."
 "In time we will say more, as and when we are able," continued the statement, which was signed by Aniston, Cox, Kudrow, LeBlanc and Schwimmer. "For now, our thoughts and our love are with Matty's family, his friends and everyone who loved him around the world."
 David Schwimmer and Matthew Perry on the 'Friends: The Reunion' 
 Credit: Terence Patrick/HBO Max 
 Each of the cast members later shared individual tributes to Perry , and in an interview last year, Aniston, 57, shared more about how the loss impacted the group.
 Advertisement Advertisement "It was so alarming and shocking, yet not shocking," she told Elle . "[We] always said, 'I hope I never get that phone call.' We miss him. He's missed. He was a brilliant human being and an extraordinary talent, loved deeply, and wanted happiness more than anything. It makes me sad that he never really achieved that because he deserved it."
